brief: A three-storey cabinet with at least three drawers.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Bases stacked at q0 r0 levels 0-2 (piece:0,0,0;half-n, piece:0,0,1;half-n, piece:0,0,2;half-n + snap:0,0,0;half-n, snap:0,0,1;half-n) plus adjoining support piece:-1,0,0;half-n / piece:-1,0,1;half-n; top closed with cover:0,0,2;half-n;top — gives 3 vertical storeys verified by get_build and measure.
Four drawers installed: drawer:0#-1,0#cut at -1,0,0 level 0, drawer:0#0,0#cut at 0,0,0 level 0, drawer:1#0,0#cut at 0,0,1 level 1, drawer:2#0,0#cut at 0,0,2 level 2 — exceeds minimum of three.

finish.summary: Three-storey vertical column at 0,0 (levels 0,1,2) plus widened base/footprint for stability, with 4 drawers distributed across all three storeys and top cover closing the cabinet. Mesh clash clear, check_build ok.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
